cross_source_observations: The recurring spatial grammar is private compact pods around shared gardens and common work, dining, and social spaces.
The visual set separates private retreat from communal participation rather than eliminating privacy.
Technical access is treated as residential infrastructure through workstation, server, fiber, node, and firewall motifs.
The garden is repeatedly central, functioning as orientation, commons, food or habitat candidate, and psychological refuge.
No image is sufficiently dimensioned or internally consistent to serve as a construction document.
Text rendering errors and inconsistent room counts must remain visible in source witnesses and be corrected only in provenance-linked descendants.
